I am 65 years old and have worked this land for 40 years. My wife and I have only two pairs of hands, so I must be practical. I have 9.5 mu in Quzhou. The wheat is already in the field from last autumn—that is my base. I keep 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that feeds us and brings steady grain income. The other 2.5 mu I plant to cotton, which I know well and which pays when prices are right. I have well water, so I can irrigate when the rains fail, but I do not waste water or money on inputs I do not need.

For the wheat already growing: I will top-dress with urea at green-up and irrigate three times this spring—green-up, jointing, and filling. I will spray twice, once for weeds and once for insects or disease if I see it. I use an improved wheat variety, not some fancy new thing I do not trust. I rotary-tilled before planting last autumn. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For summer maize: As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble without ploughing. There is no time to waste between crops, and no-tillage saves me labor. I will give it two irrigations and two pesticide applications. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

For cotton: In April I will rotary till the 2.5 mu and plant hybrid cotton seed. Cotton is thirsty and attracts bollworm, so I will irrigate three times and spray four times. I expect about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.
